title: Fourteen days' notice to quit for nonpayment of rent
requirement: A landlord may end a written lease for nonpayment with a written fourteen days' notice to quit; the lease is not ended if the tenant pays all rent due, with interest and costs, by the day the answer is due.
coverage_conditions: Any tenancy under a written lease where the tenant neglects or refuses to pay rent due.
penalty: If the nonpayment was caused by a government delay in mailing a subsistence or rental payment, the court must continue the hearing at least seven days and treat the tenancy as un-terminated if rent, interest and costs are tendered.
quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.

title: Three months' notice to determine an estate at will
requirement: Either party may end a tenancy at will on three months' written notice, or, where rent is payable more often than every three months, on notice equal to the interval between rent days or thirty days, whichever is longer.
key_value: 3 months' notice, or rent interval or 30 days, whichever is longer
coverage_conditions: Estates at will; either the landlord or the tenant may give the written notice to determine the tenancy.
citation: G.L. c. 186, § 12, notice to determine estate at will
quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer.

title: Fourteen days' notice to quit for nonpayment by a tenant at will
requirement: A landlord may end a tenancy at will for nonpayment on fourteen days' written notice; a tenant not given a similar notice in the prior twelve months keeps the tenancy by paying all rent due within ten days, and the notice must say so.
key_value: 14 days' notice; 10 days to cure, once per 12 months
coverage_conditions: Tenants at will who neglect or refuse to pay rent; the protection applies only to a tenant who got no similar notice in the preceding twelve months.
penalty: If the notice omits the required notification, the tenant's time to pay or tender rent is extended to the day the answer is due in the landlord's action for possession.
citation: G.L. c. 186, § 12, fourteen-day notice to quit for nonpayment
quoted_span:
In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy; provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, 
within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due.

title: Cap on amounts required at or before the start of a tenancy
requirement: At or before a tenancy begins, a landlord or the landlord's agent may require only first month's rent, last month's rent at the same rate, a security deposit equal to first month's rent, and the cost of a key and lock.
key_value: 1st month rent + last month rent at same rate + deposit equal to 1 month's rent + key/lock cost
coverage_conditions: Residential real property in Massachusetts; limits what a lessor or the lessor's agent may require from a tenant or prospective tenant at or before the tenancy begins.
penalty: Forfeiture of the right to retain the deposit, and treble damages plus 5% interest, court costs and reasonable attorney's fees, for a lessor who uses or enforces a lease provision conflicting with this section or seeks a waiver of it.
citation: G.L. c. 186, § 15B: upfront payments required at or before tenancy

title: Security deposit cap equal to one month's rent
requirement: A landlord may not require, and no successor may later demand, a security deposit greater than one month's rent; the deposit must be deposited under subsection (3) and the tenant given the statement of condition under subsection (2).
coverage_conditions: Residential real property in Massachusetts; security deposits received from a tenant or prospective tenant.
penalty: Forfeiture of the right to retain the deposit, and treble damages plus 5% interest, court costs and reasonable attorney's fees, for a lessor who uses or enforces a lease provision conflicting with this section or seeks a waiver of it.
quoted_span: a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)

title: Fee in lieu of a security deposit capped at one month's rent
requirement: Regulations may let a landlord and tenant agree to a fee instead of a security deposit, but the fee and any recurring payments may not total more than one month's rent, must be optional for both, and the tenant may still choose a full deposit.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies where the executive office of housing and livable communities authorizes a fee in lieu of a security deposit by regulation; it must be offered to every applicant whose application is approved.
citation: G.L. c. 186, § 15B: fee in lieu of security deposit
quoted_span: limit the total sum of the fee or recurring payments, regardless of the duration of the lease and any extensions thereto, to an amount not to exceed 1 month's rent

title: Security deposit held in a separate interest-bearing account with 5% interest
requirement: A landlord must hold a security deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account beyond creditors' claims, give a receipt within thirty days, and pay the tenant five per cent yearly interest or the lesser amount the bank paid.
coverage_conditions: Residential real property in Massachusetts; deposits held for one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy.
penalty: Failure to comply with subsection (3) entitles the tenant to the immediate return of the security deposit.
citation: G.L. c. 186, § 15B: security deposit account and interest
quoted_span: A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy.

title: Return of security deposit within thirty days of termination
requirement: Within thirty days after the tenancy ends the landlord must return the deposit or balance, may deduct only unpaid rent or water charges, tax-escalation increases and tenant damage, and must give a sworn itemized damage list for any deduction.
coverage_conditions: Tenancies at will and tenancies ending as specified in a valid written lease of residential real property in Massachusetts.
penalty: A lessor who fails to return the deposit within thirty days forfeits the right to retain any portion of it and owes three times the deposit or balance, plus 5% interest, court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
citation: G.L. c. 186, § 15B: return of security deposit and permitted deductions
quoted_span: The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof

title: Transfer of security deposit to a successor landlord with 45-day notice
requirement: A landlord who transfers the property must pass the security deposit and accrued interest to the successor, who must notify the tenant in writing within forty-five days and is liable for holding and returning the deposit.
coverage_conditions: Dwelling units where a lessor holding a security deposit transfers the interest by sale, assignment, death, appointment of a receiver or trustee in bankruptcy, or otherwise.
exemptions: Does not apply to a city or town acquiring title under chapter sixty, or to a foreclosing mortgagee or mortgagee in possession that is a financial institution chartered by the commonwealth or the United States.
penalty: A successor who does not receive the transfer assumes liability for paying the deposit to the tenant; failure to transfer or comply with subsection (5) brings three times the deposit, plus 5% interest, court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
citation: G.L. c. 186, § 15B: transfer of security deposit to successor in interest
quoted_span: The successor in interest shall, within forty-five days from the date of said transfer, notify the tenant who made such security deposit that such security deposit was transferred to him and that he is holding said security deposit.

title: Successor landlord liability for last month's rent paid in advance
requirement: On a transfer the landlord must credit the tenant's last month's rent advance and interest to the successor, who must notify the tenant in writing and is liable for the advance and interest; the outgoing landlord stays liable until then.
coverage_conditions: Dwelling units where a lessor holding rent in advance for the last month of tenancy transfers the interest by sale, assignment, death, receivership, bankruptcy trustee or otherwise.
exemptions: Liability does not apply to a city or town acquiring title under chapter sixty, or to a foreclosing mortgagee or mortgagee in possession that is a financial institution chartered by the commonwealth or by the United States.
citation: G.L. c. 186, § 15B: transfer of last month's rent advance to successor
quoted_span: In the event that the lessor fails to credit said rental advance to his successor in interest as required by this subsection, the successor in interest shall, without regard to the nature of the transfer, assume liability for crediting of the rental advance, and payment of all interest thereon to the tenant in accordance with the provisions of this section

title: Damages for reprisals against a tenant
requirement: A landlord may not threaten or take reprisals against a residential tenant for enforcing housing law, reporting code violations or joining a tenants' union; violation carries damages of one to three months' rent, or actual damages if greater, plus costs and fees.
coverage_conditions: Tenants of residential premises in Massachusetts who enforce housing law, report violations to a board or the landlord, or organize or join a tenants' union.
penalty: Damages not less than one month's rent and not more than three month's rent, or the actual damages sustained by the tenant, whichever is greater, plus costs of suit including a reasonable attorney's fee.
quoted_span: shall be liable for damages which shall not be less than one month's rent or more than three month's rent, or the actual damages sustained by the tenant, whichever is greater, and the costs of the suit, including a reasonable attorney's fee.

title: Rebuttable presumption of reprisal for termination or rent increase
requirement: A termination notice other than for nonpayment, a rent increase or a substantial change in tenancy terms within six months of a protected activity is presumed to be a reprisal, rebuttable only by clear and convincing evidence.
coverage_conditions: Tenants who commenced, proceeded with or obtained relief in such an action, exercised such rights, complained, or organized or joined a tenants' union, or where another person acted for them or in the building.
citation: G.L. c. 186, § 18: rebuttable presumption of reprisal
quoted_span: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action, exercised such rights, made such report or complaint, or organized or joined such tenants' union or within six months after any other person has taken such action or actions on behalf of the tenant or in, or relating to, the building in which the tenant resides, shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities.
